subject: Banking
title: Chime: America's Biggest Neobank
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Chime: America's Biggest Neobank.

hook.text: Chime has 22 million customers and zero branches. It earns money from interchange fees, not overdraft penalties.

buildup.text: Chime offers no-fee checking, early direct deposit (2 days), and a credit-building secured card. All through an app.

discovery.text: Chime's revenue model flips traditional banking. Instead of charging users fees.

twist.text: Chime is not technically a bank. Bancorp Bank and Stride Bank hold the deposits.

climax.text: Chime proved that banking without fees attracts millions. Align revenue with usage instead of punishing overdrafts.

punchline.text: 22 million users. No fees. Revenue from swipe fees, not penalties.

quiz.question: How does Chime make money?
options: Interchange fees earned when customers use their cards

details.summary: Chime grew to over 20 million customers by offering fee-free banking, early direct deposit, and automatic savings features, targeting Americans frustrated with traditional bank fees and minimum balance requirements.
details.whyItMatters: Chime proved that millions of Americans would switch to a digital-only bank for better economics. Its growth pressured traditional banks to reduce fees and improve digital offerings.
takeaways: Chime has over 20 million customers with no physical branches
Early direct deposit, up to two days faster, is a signature feature
Revenue comes primarily from interchange fees on debit transactions

faq.question: How does Chime make money without charging fees?
faq.answer: Chime earns interchange fees every time a customer uses their debit card, typically 1 to 2 percent of the transaction. With 20 million active users making daily purchases, these small fees generate substantial revenue at scale.

faq.question: Is Chime actually a bank?
faq.answer: Technically, Chime is a financial technology company, not a chartered bank. It partners with Bancorp Bank and Stride Bank, which hold the banking licenses and provide FDIC insurance on deposits. Chime provides the customer-facing technology.
